brand: The Residual Stream · EP 01 · How it began

lines.text: Vera, did chatbots always read like this?
No. For decades, programs read text through a keyhole: one word at a time.
And forgot most of what came before?
Mostly. Each step in this story makes the keyhole wider.
So what was the first step?
2013: word vectors. Words become lists of numbers that capture meaning.
lines.say: Twenty thirteen: word vectors. Words become lists of numbers that capture meaning.

lines.text: King minus man plus woman lands near queen.
Words with directions. Fancy.
Then machines learned to translate?
2014: sequence to sequence. It squeezes the whole sentence into one vector, then writes the translation from it.
lines.say: Twenty fourteen: sequence to sequence. It squeezes the whole sentence into one vector, then writes the translation from it.

lines.text: A whole sentence in one vector?
Exactly the problem. On long sentences, details get lost.
So how do you stop the squeeze?
Attention, also 2014. The decoder looks back at every word and picks which ones to focus on.
lines.say: Attention, also twenty fourteen. The decoder looks back at every word, and picks which ones to focus on.

lines.text: No more single vector!
The transformer. It dropped recurrence and kept only attention, so it trains in parallel on GPUs.
lines.say: The transformer. It dropped recurrence, and kept only attention, so it trains in parallel on G P Us.

lines.text: The T in ChatGPT?
lines.say: The T, in Chat G P T?

lines.text: That's the one. And it kept improving as it was made bigger.
Can I see the whole story?
Pick one of the three acts on the timeline in the How it began chapter.
Sixty years of ideas. I'll skim the highlights.
